author: speculatingwook
body:
## 📌 개요  
* `Member` 엔티티의 생성 방식을 Builder에서 정적 팩토리 메서드로 전환하고, 각 필드에 대한 유효성 검증 및 DB 제약조건을 명시했습니다.

## 🛠️ 작업 내용  
- [x] `@Builder` 제거 및 `static of()` 정적 팩토리 메서드 도입  
- [x] `@NotBlank`, `@Email`, `@Size`, `@NotNull` 등 유효성 어노테이션 추가  
- [x] `@Column(nullable = false)`, `unique = true` 등 DB 제약조건 추가  

### 정적 팩토리 메서드 도입  

* `@Builder` 어노테이션을 제거하고, 보다 명확한 생성 방식을 위해 `Member.of()` 정적 팩토리 메서드를 도입했습니다.  
* 추후 생성자 변경이 필요한 경우, 유지보수 측면에서 유연하게 대처할 수 있도록 구조를 개선했습니다.

### 필드 제약조건 추가  

* 각 필드에 대해 적절한 유효성 검증 및 DB 제약조건을 추가했습니다.  
  - `name`: `@NotBlank`, `@Size(min=2, max=50)`  
  - `email`: `@Email`, `@NotBlank`, `@Column(unique=true)`  
  - `password`: `@NotBlank`, `@Size(min=8)`  
  - `birth`: `@NotNull`  

## 📌 차후 계획 (Optional)  
* 정적 팩토리 메서드 기반의 유효성 검증 및 테스트 케이스 보완 예정  
* 다른 도메인 엔티티에도 동일한 생성 패턴을 적용하여 일관성 확보 예정

## 📌 기타 참고 사항  
* Builder 제거로 인해 코드 사용 방식이 바뀐 부분이 있어, 기존 사용처 확인 및 리팩토링을 진행했습니다.
* 유효성 어노테이션은 런타임 검증용이며, `@Valid`가 적용되는 계층에서만 동작하므로, 컨트롤러나 서비스 계층의 유효성 처리 여부 확인 바랍니다.

---

#### 🙏🏻 아래와 같이 PR을 리뷰해주세요.  
- 코드의 생성 방식이 정적 팩토리 메서드로 일관성 있게 바뀌었는지 확인해주세요.  
- 각 필드에 명시된 제약조건이 도메인 요구사항과 일치하는지 검토해주세요.  
- 기존 Builder 패턴을 사용한 코드가 있다면 새 방식으로 잘 이관되었는지도 확인 부탁드립니다.

Closes #12

author: jimmy1wu
body:
- fix the remaining fips 140-3 failures in wsscxf.3 fat via java security constraints
- remove `jdk.xml.dsig.secureValidationPolicy` workaround and fix the disallowed http://www.w3.org/2000/09/xmldsig#sha1 the correct way
    - turns out wss4j uses their own `org.apache.jcp.xml.dsig.internal.dom.XMLDSigRI` provider instead of using the `org.jcp.xml.dsig.internal.dom.XMLDSigRI` provider
- added comments with TODO's

Notes:
- using SunRsaSign:
    - the providers that include SHA1withRSA are SunRsaSign, SunJSSE, SunMSCAPI, and OracleUcrypto.
    - i decided to go with adding SunRsaSign instead of using SunJSSE because the docs say
`The SunRsaSign provider was introduced in JDK 1.3 as an enhanced replacement for the RSA signatures in the SunJSSE provider.`
    - https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/technotes/guides/security/SunProviders.html#SunRsaSignProvider

author: clafollett
body:
## Fix Premature Release PR Creation

**Part of:** Issue #68 - CI/CD pipeline fixes

## Problem
Release-plz was creating release PRs immediately after any commit to main, before the CI workflow (tests, builds, security audit) could complete. This led to premature release attempts.

## Solution
Changed the release-plz workflow to use `workflow_run` trigger that waits for the "CI" workflow to complete successfully.

## Changes
- **Trigger**: `on: push` → `on: workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"]`
- **Condition**: Only run if `github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success'`
- **Flow**: Push → CI → (if success) → Release-plz PR

## Benefits
- No more premature release PRs
- Release PRs only created after code passes all quality gates
- Maintains automatic release detection but with proper dependency ordering

## Testing
Cleared GitHub Actions cache before this change to ensure fresh state for version detection.

클라이언트가 특정 게시글(Post Read)을 조회하면, 서버는 Redis를 통해 중복 조회 여부를 판단합니다.

TTL 10분인 키 view:member:{memberUuid}:post:{postUuid}로 조회 여부를 기록합니다.

중복 조회가 아니라면 Kafka에 post-view-topic 이벤트를 발행합니다.

Kafka Consumer는 해당 이벤트를 수신하여 Redis에 집계용 키 aggregate:post:view:{postUuid}의 값을 증가시킵니다.

Spring Batch 스케줄러가 1분마다 Redis에 쌓인 view 카운트를 MongoDB로 동기화합니다.

동기화 후 Redis 키는 삭제 처리됩니다.

# [YA-11] Mobile-First Homepage Enhancement with Interactive UI Overlays v1.1.0

## Overview
<!-- Provide a brief description of what this PR accomplishes and why -->
This PR enhances the portfolio homepage with comprehensive UI overlays that guide users on how to interact with the 3D demo experience. The implementation focuses on mobile-first responsive design while maintaining the core Three.js canvas functionality. Users now receive clear visual cues and instructions for navigating the interactive 3D environment through intuitive overlay components.

## 🔍 JIRA Ticket
<!-- Link to the JIRA ticket(s) this PR addresses -->
- [YA-11](https://yobertyalej.atlassian.net/browse/YA-11) Mobile-First Homepage Enhancement with Interactive UI Overlays

## 🧩 Type of Change
<!-- Mark the relevant type(s) with an 'x' -->
- [x] `feat`: New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [x] `fix`: Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] `docs`: Documentation only changes
- [ ] `style`: Changes that do not affect the meaning of the code
- [x] `refactor`: Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
- [ ] `perf`: Code change that improves performance
- [ ] `test`: Adding missing tests or correcting existing tests
- [ ] `chore`: Changes to the build process or auxiliary tools
- [ ] `i18n`: Internationalization changes
- [ ] `ai`: AI component modifications
- [ ] `exp`: Experimental changes

## 🔄 Scope
<!-- Mark the relevant scope(s) with an 'x' -->
- [ ] `core`: Core portfolio components
- [ ] `blog`: Blog system
- [x] `ui`: User interface components
- [x] `three`: 3D visualizations
- [ ] `playground`: AI Playground
- [ ] `i18n`: Internationalization

## 🚀 Changes
<!-- Detail the specific changes made in this PR -->

### Added
<!-- New features or components added -->
- **HeroOverlay**: Instructions panel in top-left corner with interaction badges (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, look for orange hotspots)
- **InteractiveHotspots**: Orange pulsating points overlaying the 3D scene with tooltips showing available interactions
- **NavigationGuide**: Right sidebar panel displaying available views (General, Arcade Machine, About Screen)
- **WelcomeTour**: 3-step onboarding experience for new visitors with localStorage integration
- **MobileGuide**: Collapsible bottom panel optimized for touch devices and mobile navigation
- **Bidirectional communication** between UI overlays and 3D scene via props system
- **Debug components** for development (`HotspotDebug`, `ViewStateDebug`)

### Changed
<!-- Existing functionality that was modified -->
- **DeskScene component** now accepts communication props (`onViewChange`, `currentView`, `onHotspotHover`, `onHotspotPositions`)
- **Mobile-first responsive design** with optimized camera positions and scaling for different screen sizes
- **Enhanced camera control system** with device-specific configurations
- **Level component** updated to support position debugging and interaction callbacks

### Fixed
<!-- Bugs or issues that were resolved -->
- **Critical infinite loop issue** caused by bidirectional useEffect communication patterns
- **Three.js color errors** - replaced string colors with proper hex values (`"transparent"` → `{0x000000}` with opacity)
- **ReferenceError**: Fixed variable initialization order in DeskScene component
- **Event propagation issues** - added `stopPropagation()` to all interactive elements
- **State management stability** using proper `useCallback` patterns

### Removed
<!-- Features, components, or code that was removed -->
- **Debug controls** completely disabled for production deployment
- **Development-only imports** commented out or removed
- **Console.log statements** cleaned up for production build
- **Unused debugging hooks** and commented code blocks

## 📊 Testing
<!-- Describe the testing performed to verify your changes -->
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Accessibility verification

**Manual Testing Performed:**
- ✅ Desktop responsive design (1920x1080, 1366x768)
- ✅ Mobile responsive design (iPhone, Android various sizes)
- ✅ Touch interactions on mobile devices
- ✅ Hotspot positioning and clicking functionality
- ✅ Camera transitions between views
- ✅ Welcome tour localStorage persistence
- ✅ Mobile guide collapse/expand functionality

## 📝 Semantic Versioning Impact
<!-- How this PR affects the versioning. E.g., "This is a MINOR change as it adds new functionality without breaking changes." -->
- Version bump: `MINOR` (x.y.z)
- New version: **v1.1.0**

This is a MINOR version bump as it adds significant new UI functionality and mobile-first enhancements while maintaining full backward compatibility with existing Three.js implementation.

## 🧠 AI Integration
<!-- If applicable, describe any AI components or LLM utilization in this PR -->
This PR enhances the "AI Augmented Developer" theme by providing better user guidance to interact with AI-powered demos within the 3D environment, particularly the arcade machine and interactive screens.

## 🌐 Internationalization Considerations
<!-- If applicable, describe i18n implications of this change -->
All UI text is currently in Spanish. Future i18n implementation should consider:
- Button text in overlays
- Instruction text in HeroOverlay
- Tour step descriptions in WelcomeTour
- Mobile guide content

## 🔄 Next Steps
<!-- Future work related to this PR -->
- Implement analytics tracking for user interactions with hotspots
- Add animation transitions between overlay states
- Consider A/B testing different instruction methodologies
- Implement keyboard navigation for accessibility
- Add more interactive elements to the 3D scene

## 📸 Screenshots/Videos
<!-- Add before/after screenshots or videos if applicable -->
<details>
<summary>Before</summary>

Plain 3D scene without user guidance - users had to discover interactions by trial and error
</details>

<details>
<summary>After</summary>

Enhanced UI with:
- Clear instruction overlays
- Visual hotspot indicators
- Mobile-optimized navigation
- Step-by-step onboarding tour
</details>

## ✅ PR Checklist
<!-- Mark completed items with an 'x' -->
- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation has been updated
- [ ] Tests added/updated and all tests pass
- [x] No new warnings introduced
- [ ] Version has been updated in package.json
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md has been updated
- [x] Responsive design verified (if UI changes)
- [x] Accessibility standards met (if UI changes)
- [x] Performance impact considered
- [x] Code is self-reviewing (comments, variable names, etc.)

## 📋 Additional Notes
<!-- Any other information that might be helpful -->

**Architecture Decision:**
The implementation uses a bidirectional communication pattern between the 3D scene and UI overlays. This allows real-time synchronization of hotspot positions and view states while maintaining clean separation of concerns.

**Performance Considerations:**
- Hotspot position calculations are optimized with `useCallback` and `useMemo`
- Debug components are conditionally rendered only in development
- Mobile-specific optimizations reduce render complexity on smaller devices

**Critical Bug Resolution:**
The infinite loop issue was caused by circular `useEffect` dependencies. This was resolved by implementing a callback-based communication pattern instead of reactive state synchronization.

author: pencil
body:
This PR optimizes the handling of empty `Chain` or `Group` workflows. Instead of scheduling a noop task and relying on the middleware to process completion callbacks, this change processes them directly within the `Workflow.run` method when there is no delay. This avoids an unnecessary round trip to the broker.

## Why do we even support empty `Chain`s and `Group`s?

Empty chains and groups are common when created programmatically:

```python
Chain(
  Group(*[do_a_bunch_of_work.message(id) for id in work_items]),
  finalize_work.message(),
)
```

In this example, `work_items` might be empty, in which case `finalize_work` should run immediately.

author: krzysz00
body:
This commit adds a descriptor attribute - #iree_gpu.scaled_mma_layout -
for MMAs that take "scale" operands and tests for its lowering
from DistributeInnerTiledToLanes and afterwards.

This descriptor takes four input operands - the lleft-hand side of the
matrix, the LHS scales, the right-hand side, and the RHS scales, in
that order. The operation has one accumulator.

Scaled MMAs are, like MMA intrinsics, represented by an enum, which
litss out the available intrinsics (currenvtly, we only have AMD's
MI-350). However, unlike with MMA intrinsics, the input and output
types are given in the scaled_mma_layout attribute itself. This is
because these scaled MMAs support arbitrary pairs of left- and
right-hand side types from {f4E2M1FN, f6E3M2FN, f6E3M2FN, f8E4M3FN,
f8E5M2}, so listing out all the combinations would take up a lot of
space and produce a large number of nearly-identical cases in the
descriotor logic.

This inner tiled operation treats the k values that have distinct
scales and the "block" (the B (currently always 32) values that share
a common scale) as separate reduction dimensions. This means that the
scale operands, in effect, don't have a block dimension. This also
means that models where the block size is larger than 32 can be
supported by tiling across the scale dimension.

The following work is not yet implemented:
- ContretizeMmaShapes has not yet been generalized to arbitrary inner
tiled ops. This will be needed to correctly lower the 32x32x64
intrinsic, which has an outer dimension on the accumulator.
- Lowering configuration logic and PackToIntrinsics have not been
addressed

Note that this PR does contain a few code changes. One is declaring
the vector unrolling logic to be safe for non-MMA inner_tiled ops. The
other is a bug fix to basisFromSizesStrides(), which used an incorrect
tiebreaking strategy for multiple dimensions that had the same
stride (now it's ties broken by the length of the dimension and _then_
its position in the list).

- Added Cursor IDE configuration files (.mdc format) to improve development experience
- These files provide project-specific knowledge and guidelines for Cursor IDE

## Changes
- Added 7 new .mdc files in `.cursor/` directory:
  - `coding-standards.mdc` - Coding conventions and best practices
  - `commands.mdc` - Common command reference
  - `git-workflow.mdc` - Git operation guidelines
  - `knowledge-management.mdc` - AI knowledge management documentation
  - `project-overview.mdc` - Project overview and instructions
  - `tech-stack.mdc` - Technology stack specifications
  - `testing.mdc` - Testing guidelines and best practices

## Purpose
These configuration files help Cursor IDE understand the project context better, providing:
- Better code suggestions aligned with project standards
- Quick access to common commands and workflows
- Consistent development practices across the team

## Test plan
- [x] Verified all .mdc files are properly formatted
- [x] Checked that files contain accurate project information
- [x] Ensured no sensitive information is included

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This change hardens all [`BufferedReader#readLine()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/BufferedReader.html#readLine--) operations against memory exhaustion.

There is no way to call `readLine()` safely since it is, by its nature, a read that must be terminated by the stream provider. Furthermore, a stream of data provided by an untrusted source could lead to a denial of service attack, as attackers can provide an infinite stream of bytes until the process runs out of memory.

Fixing it is straightforward using an API which limits the amount of expected characters to some sane limit. This is what our changes look like:

```diff
+ import io.github.pixee.security.BoundedLineReader;
  ...
  BufferedReader reader = getReader();
- String line = reader.readLine(); // unlimited read, can lead to DoS
+ String line = BoundedLineReader.readLine(reader, 5_000_000); // limited to 5MB
```

author: pixeebot[bot]
body:
This codemod sandboxes calls to [`requests.get`](https://requests.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api/#requests.get) to be more resistant to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks.

Most of the time when you make a `GET` request to a URL, you're intending to reference an HTTP endpoint, like an internal microservice. However, URLs can point to local file system files, a Gopher stream in your local network, a JAR file on a remote Internet site, and all kinds of other unexpected and undesirable outcomes. When the URL values are influenced by attackers, they can trick your application into fetching internal resources, running malicious code, or otherwise harming the system.
Consider the following code for a Flask app:

```python
from flask import Flask, request
import requests

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/request-url")
def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
    resp = requests.get(url)
    ...
```

In this case, an attacker could supply a value like `"http://169.254.169.254/user-data/"` and attempt to access user information.

Our changes introduce sandboxing around URL creation that force developers to specify some boundaries on the types of URLs they expect to create:

```diff
  from flask import Flask, request
- import requests
+ from security import safe_requests

  app = Flask(__name__)

  @app.route("/request-url")
  def request_url():
    url = request.args["loc"]
-   resp = requests.get(url)
+   resp = safe_requests.get(url)
    ...
```

This change alone reduces attack surface significantly because the default behavior of `safe_requests.get` raises a `SecurityException` if
a user attempts to access a known infrastructure location, unless specifically disabled.


If you have feedback on this codemod, [please let us know](mailto:feedback@pixee.ai)!

## F.A.Q. 

### Why does this codemod require a Pixee dependency?

We always prefer to use built-in Python functions or one from a well-known and trusted community dependency. However, we cannot find any such control. If you know of one, [please let us know](https://ask.pixee.ai/feedback).

### Why is this codemod marked as Merge After Cursory Review?

By default, the protection only weaves in 2 checks, which we believe will not cause any issues with the vast majority of code:
1. The given URL must be HTTP/HTTPS.
2. The given URL must not point to a "well-known infrastructure target", which includes things like AWS Metadata Service endpoints, and internal routers (e.g., 192.168.1.1) which are common targets of attacks.

However, on rare occasions an application may use a URL protocol like "file://" or "ftp://" in backend or middleware code.

If you want to allow those protocols, change the incoming PR to look more like this and get the best security possible:

```diff
-resp = requests.get(url)
+resp = safe_requests.get(url, allowed_protocols=("ftp",))
```

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. However, we were unable to automatically add the dependency to your project. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. You may need to manually add this dependency to the proper location in your project.

### Manual Installation

For `setup.py`:
```diff
 install_requires=[
+    "security==1.3.1",
 ],
```

For `pyproject.toml` (using `setuptools`):
```diff
 [project]

+    "security==1.3.1",
 ]
```

For `setup.cfg`:
```diff

 install_requires =
+    security==1.3.1
```

For `requirements.txt`:
```diff
+security==1.3.1
```

For more information on adding dependencies to `setuptools` projects, see [the setuptools documentation](https://setuptools.pypa.io/en/latest/userguide/dependency_management.html#declaring-required-dependency). 

If you are using another build system, please refer to the documentation for that system to determine how to add dependencies.

# Inlining for CU Reduction

## Summary
Implemented `#[inline(always)]` annotations to eliminate function call overhead and enable compiler optimizations. 

## Changes
- **Core Trait Methods**: Added inline annotations to all ReadableAccount and WritableAccount trait implementations including key(), lamports(), data(), assign(), and realloc() methods
- **Account Validation**: Inlined all FromAccountInfo::try_from_info implementations across account types
- **Generated Code**: Modified macro code generation to emit inline annotations for context validation and trace_account methods
- **Instruction Dispatch**: Upgraded instruction handler invoke() methods from #[inline] to #[inline(always)] and inlined argument processing functions
- **Utility Functions**: Inlined utility trait methods for account operations, lamport transfers, and system program interactions
- **Error Handling**: Inlined error creation and conversion functions while preserving error formatting to avoid binary bloat

## Impact
Total improvement of 128+ CU across all instructions without altering repo functionality.

body:
Python's `pickle` module is notoriouly insecure. While it is very useful for serializing and deserializing Python objects, it is not safe to use `pickle` to load data from untrusted sources. This is because `pickle` can execute arbitrary code when loading data. This can be exploited by an attacker to execute arbitrary code on your system. Unlike `yaml` there is no concept of a "safe" loader in `pickle`. Therefore, it is recommended to avoid `pickle` and to use a different serialization format such as `json` or `yaml` when working with untrusted data.

However, if you must use `pickle` to load data from an untrusted source, we recommend using the open-source `fickling` library. `fickling` is a drop-in replacement for `pickle` that validates the data before loading it and checks for the possibility of code execution. This makes it much safer (although still not entirely safe) to use `pickle` to load data from untrusted sources.

This codemod replaces calls to `pickle.load` with `fickling.load` in Python code. It also adds an import statement for `fickling` if it is not already present. 

The changes look like the following:
```diff
- import pickle
+ import fickling
 
- data = pickle.load(file)
+ data = fickling.load(file)
```

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. 

This package provides analysis of pickled data to help identify potential security vulnerabilities. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.

body:
This PR completes the Java `SingleThreadEngine` implementation to match the functionality of the JavaScript `Engine` class, implementing all missing methods and ensuring behavioral equivalence between the two implementations.

## Changes Made

### Core Engine Method Implementations
- **`setInitialCharge`**: Sets initial charge values with proper recharge calculation logic
- **`recharge`**: Sets recharge parameters and triggers recalculations  
- **`retire`**: Sets retirement rates and triggers retirement recalculation
- **`recycle`**: Sets recycling parameters (recovery, yield, displacement) and triggers recalculations
- **`equals`**: Sets GHG/energy intensities and triggers emission recalculations
- **`cap`/`floor`**: Implements stream value capping/flooring with displacement support
- **`replace`**: Implements substance replacement functionality

### Recalculation Methods
Implemented all `recalc*` methods that were previously placeholders:
- **`recalcPopulationChange`**: Equipment population recalculation based on sales and recharge
- **`recalcConsumption`**: GHG and energy consumption recalculation  
- **`recalcSales`**: Manufacturing and import sales recalculation with recycling
- **`recalcRetire`**: Equipment retirement and end-of-life emissions
- **`recalcRechargeEmissions`**: Emissions from equipment recharging
- **`recalcEolEmissions`**: End-of-life emission calculations

### Helper Methods
- **`calculateRechargeVolume`**: Calculates recharge volume for current scope
- **`changeStreamWithoutReportingUnits`**: Internal stream changes without unit tracking
- **`getShouldSubtractRecharge`**: Logic for recharge calculation behavior

### State Management Improvements
Added clear methods to `OverridingConverterStateGetter`:
- **`clearPopulation()`**: Clear population override
- **`clearVolume()`**: Clear volume override  
- **`clearAmortizedUnitVolume()`**: Clear amortized unit volume override

These methods properly handle state transitions that previously used `null` assignments.

### Test Enhancements
Enhanced `SingleThreadEngineTest` to better match JavaScript test coverage:
- Added "gets years reverse" test for constructor argument ordering
- Enhanced scope management test to verify scope changes
- Added comprehensive comments comparing test behaviors

### Documentation
Added detailed comparison comments across all major engine components explaining key differences between Java and JavaScript implementations:

- **BigDecimal vs JavaScript floats** for numerical precision
- **Optional pattern vs null/undefined** checking
- **Typed exceptions vs string throwing**
- **Java collections vs JavaScript objects**
- **Static typing vs dynamic typing**
- **Clear methods vs null assignments**

## Test Results
- ✅ All 164 Java tests passing
- ✅ All 338 JavaScript tests passing
- ✅ No functional regressions introduced

## Key Differences from JavaScript
The Java implementation maintains identical simulation logic while using:
- `BigDecimal` for numerical stability instead of JavaScript floats
- Strong typing and proper exception handling
- Java collection patterns instead of JavaScript objects
- Optional pattern for nullable state management

## Note on Remaining Work
- 18 checkstyle warnings remain (mainly line length >100 chars)
- `getResults()` method awaits `EngineResult` Java conversion in future PR
- All core simulation functionality is complete and equivalent

Fixes #224.

This pull request introduces several changes aimed at improving dependency management, adding comprehensive unit tests, and updating package requirements. The most significant updates include replacing the `easyrdf/easyrdf` library with `sweetrdf/easyrdf`, adding new unit test files to validate various functions, and including a sample RDF dataset for testing. Below is a breakdown of the key changes:

## Changes
### Dependency Updates
* Updated `composer.json` to replace `easyrdf/easyrdf` with `sweetrdf/easyrdf` for RDF processing and retained `nikic/fast-route` for routing. This ensures compatibility with newer versions and improves library support.

### Unit Test Additions
* Added `tests/FetchAndProcessCGIKeywordsTest.php` to test the `fetchAndProcessCGIKeywords` function using mocked HTTP responses and a local RDF dataset. This validates the hierarchical structure of CGI keywords.
* Added `tests/ParseAffiliationAndRorIdsTest.php` to test `parseAffiliationData` and `parseRorIds` functions with various input scenarios, ensuring proper parsing of affiliations and ROR IDs.
* Added `tests/ValidationFunctionsTest.php` to cover multiple validation functions, including field requirements, array dependencies, contributor dependencies, keyword entries, spatial-temporal coverage, and funding references. This ensures robust validation logic across different data types.

### Test Dataset
* Added `tests/datasets/simplelithology.rdf`, a sample RDF dataset, for testing hierarchical RDF parsing in `FetchAndProcessCGIKeywordsTest`. This provides a controlled environment for verifying RDF-related functionality.

author: nivihelen99
body:
This commit introduces a generic, thread-safe LRU (Least Recently Used) Cache component, `LRUCache<Key, Value>`, implemented as a header-only C++ template.

The `LRUCache` provides O(1) average time complexity for core operations (`put`, `get`, `erase`, `contains`) by using `std::unordered_map` for quick lookups and `std::list` to maintain the LRU order of items.

Key Features:
- Configurable maximum capacity (`max_size`).
- Thread safety is ensured through the use of `std::mutex` protecting all public methods.
- An optional `EvictCallback` can be provided to the constructor, which is invoked when an item is evicted due to capacity constraints.
- `get(key)` returns `std::optional<Value>`, promoting the accessed item to the Most Recently Used (MRU) position.
- `put(key, value)` inserts or updates an item, also promoting it to the MRU position. If capacity is exceeded, the Least Recently Used (LRU) item is evicted.
- `erase(key)` removes an item and returns `true` if successful.
- `contains(key)` checks for an item's existence without altering its LRU status.
- `clear()`, `size()`, and `empty()` methods are provided for cache management.
- The implementation is header-only (`include/lru_cache.h`).

Unit tests using Google Test (`tests/lru_cache_test.cpp`) have been added, covering:
- Basic operations (put, get, erase, clear, contains).
- LRU eviction policy and MRU promotion on access/update.
- Eviction callback functionality.
- Thread safety through concurrent operations.
- Usage with custom key/value types (requiring `std::hash` specialization for custom keys if not standard).

An example program (`examples/lru_cache_example.cpp`) demonstrates the usage of the `LRUCache` with various features.

CMake build files (`CMakeLists.txt` and `tests/CMakeLists.txt`) have been updated to:
- Compile the new example.
- Build and register the new tests.
- Link necessary threading libraries for both tests and examples that use the LRUCache.

messing around with some chirps-gefs classes/methods for downloading, loading, and processing data.  The downloading and loading seem to be  working somewhat well when I run interactively from the beginning [quarto book chapter chirps-gef](https://github.com/OCHA-DAP/ds-aa-cub-hurricanes/blob/chirps-gefs/book_cub_hurricanes/chirps_gefs.qmd) - everything after the `## TBD` header (line 237) can be completely ignored for now.  In fact I don't see any point in going over the chapter at all yet until we're able to get the min-reprex (discussed below) to be triggered from DB:

I've been trying to see if i can get a simple small download script running  via a DataBricks job. This is the script: [test_download_chirps_gefs.py](https://github.com/OCHA-DAP/ds-aa-cub-hurricanes/blob/chirps-gefs/test_download_chirps_gefs.py) in the root directory. The script runs locally, but so far haven't ironed out some of the DBricks stuff. So far on that front I've

1.  created a job which should run the test_download_cihrps_gefs.py script. You should be able to view runs under `Data Engineering` -> `Job Runs`. 
2. Created a work-space that connects to the repo. Here i'm able to run notebooks and scripts and should be able to just run the script directly (not as a job), but so far no luck yet. After doing the various steps you will see in the update - this method is almost working, but now hitting errors which seem to be caused by not having the right env vars in the DB environment See update section below.

 For now **ignore** `class ChirpsGefsProcessor` as that is basically a placeholder just to calculate mean values -- and not fully working yet.

## Update on loading local modules in Data Bricks

Update: as @t-downing mentioned, importing custom modules in databricks does seem to involve an absurd amount of pain. I did make some progress however, and it seems to be working, basically by:

1. create a whl file on local with `build` package:

```
python -m pip install build
python -m build
```
2. Go to DB workspace click the 3 dots upload file.
3. Then create a notebook where you move the whl file to dbfs 
```
import shutil
import os

# Create the destination directory if it does not exist
os.makedirs("/dbfs/tmp", exist_ok=True)

shutil.copyfile(
    "/Workspace/Users/{username}@{userdomain}.org/ds-aa-cub-hurricanes/src-0.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
    "/dbfs/tmp/src-0.0.0-py3-none-any.whl" # name of wheel file (in my case this was the file)
)
```
4. in same notebook you can pip install the whl file from dbfs with something like ( i think this part  and probabl even step 3 could be put in `init script`).
```
%pip install /dbfs/tmp/src-0.0.0-py3-none-any.whl
```

The problem now seems to be that the pre-configured env variables we have in our DataBricks compute clusters are not name correctly for ocha-stratus (particularly for dev access)  as listed in the [ocha-stratus documentation](https://ocha-stratus.readthedocs.io/en/latest/installation.html#environment-configuration) --- so this seems to be causing the next set of errors/issues.  @hannahker  - are you able to adjust the env vars that are pre-loaded w/ dbricks compute clusters so that ocha-stratus can properly load from blob etc?  I see for example that DBricks creates a var called: `DSCI_AZ_SAS_DEV` when according to our ocha-stratus documentation it should be: `DSCI_AZ_BLOB_DEV_SAS`

Many developers are not necessarily aware that the `isinstance` and `issubclass` builtin methods can accept a tuple of classes to match. This means that there is a lot of code that uses boolean expressions such as `isinstance(x, str) or isinstance(x, bytes)` instead of the simpler expression `isinstance(x, (str, bytes))`.

This codemod simplifies the boolean expressions where possible which leads to cleaner and more concise code.

The changes from this codemod look like this:

```diff
  x = 'foo'
```

```bash
├── .github/                          # GitHub workflows for CI/CD tests
├── configs/                          # Training and evaluation configuration YAMLs
├── experiments/                      # Scripts and setups for running controlled experiments
├── results/                          # Output from experiments: plots, logs, metrics, etc.
├── scripts/                          # Bash scripts for launching jobs (e.g. on WatGPU)
├── simglucose/                       # Custom fork of simglucose package
├── src/
│   ├── agents/                       # Creating, loading, and managing agents
│   ├── environments/		      # Custom Gym environments and reward functions
```

author: robco
body:
## Overview

This PR significantly improves the test coverage of the Czech TV EPG Grabber project by adding comprehensive test suites for three critical modules that previously had insufficient coverage.

## Coverage Improvements

| Module | Before | After | Improvement |
|--------|--------|-------|-----------|
| **cli.py** | 0% | 99% | +99 percentage points |
| **sources/blesk_cz.py** | 21% | 100% | +79 percentage points |
| **sources/centrum_cz.py** | 37% | 100% | +63 percentage points |
| **Overall Project** | 58% | 94% | +36 percentage points |

## New Test Files Added

### 1. `tests/test_cli.py` (34 tests)
Complete testing of the command-line interface including:
- ✅ Argument parsing for all CLI options (`--config`, `--output`, `--source`, etc.)
- ✅ Programme queries (current, at-time, day-schedule)
- ✅ Channel listing in multiple formats (table, JSON, CSV)
- ✅ Blesk-specific features (programme tips, details)
- ✅ Error handling and validation
- ✅ Short option aliases (`-c`, `-o`, `-s`, `-d`, `-v`)

### 2. `tests/test_blesk_cz.py` (31 tests)
Comprehensive testing of the Blesk.cz EPG source including:
- ✅ API initialization and configuration
- ✅ Category and channel fetching with logo URLs
- ✅ Programme fetching with enhanced details and images
- ✅ Programme tips and detailed information retrieval
- ✅ Time parsing and calculation utilities
- ✅ Error handling for all API endpoints
- ✅ Integration workflow testing

### 3. `tests/test_centrum_cz.py` (33 tests)
Complete testing of the Centrum.cz EPG source including:
- ✅ API initialization and configuration
- ✅ Channel and programme fetching
- ✅ URL construction and parameter handling
- ✅ Logo URL generation
- ✅ Error handling for various network scenarios
- ✅ Edge cases and performance testing

## Testing Methodology

### Quality Assurance
- **Mocking Strategy**: All external API calls are mocked using `unittest.mock`
- **Error Coverage**: Comprehensive testing of network errors, API failures, and edge cases
- **Performance**: All 220 tests complete in under 4 seconds
- **Isolation**: Each test is independent and produces deterministic results

### Error Scenarios Tested
- Network timeouts and connection failures
- HTTP errors (404, 500, etc.)
- Invalid JSON responses
- Missing or malformed data
- Invalid input parameters
- Edge cases and boundary conditions

## Documentation

Added `COMPREHENSIVE_TEST_COVERAGE.md` with detailed documentation including:
- Module-by-module coverage breakdown
- Test class descriptions and coverage
- Testing methodology and quality metrics
- Benefits achieved and future recommendations

## Benefits

### Development Benefits
- **Regression Prevention**: Comprehensive tests prevent code regressions
- **Refactoring Safety**: High coverage enables safe code refactoring
- **Bug Detection**: Tests catch issues before production deployment
- **Documentation**: Tests serve as executable documentation

### Quality Metrics
- **Total Tests**: 220 (up from 122)
- **New Tests Added**: 98
- **Test Success Rate**: 100%
- **Fast Execution**: <4 seconds for full suite

## Testing

All tests pass successfully:
```bash
$ pytest --cov=epg_grabber
============== 220 passed in 3.92s ==============
TOTAL coverage: 94%
```

## Breaking Changes

None. This PR only adds tests and documentation without modifying any existing functionality.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added for new functionality
- [x] All tests pass
- [x] Code coverage improved significantly
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] No breaking changes
- [x] Follows existing code style and patterns

## Pre-requisites

---

### **Please note that at this time we are only accepting new starter workflows for Code Scanning. Updates to existing starter workflows are fine.**

---

## Tasks

**For _all_ workflows, the workflow:**

- [ ] Should be contained in a `.yml` file with the language or platform as its filename, in lower, [_kebab-cased_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kebab_case) format (for example, [`docker-image.yml`](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/blob/main/ci/docker-image.yml)).  Special characters should be removed or replaced with words as appropriate (for example, "dotnet" instead of ".NET").
- [ ] Should use sentence case for the names of workflows and steps (for example, "Run tests").
- [ ] Should be named _only_ by the name of the language or platform (for example, "Go", not "Go CI" or "Go Build").
- [ ] Should include comments in the workflow for any parts that are not obvious or could use clarification.
- [ ] Should specify least privileged [permissions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#modifying-the-permissions-for-the-github_token) for `GITHUB_TOKEN` so that the workflow runs successfully.

**For _CI_ workflows, the workflow:**

- [ ] Should be preserved under [the `ci` directory](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/tree/main/ci).
- [ ] Should include a matching `ci/properties/*.properties.json` file (for example, [`ci/properties/docker-publish.properties.json`](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/blob/main/ci/properties/docker-publish.properties.json)).
- [ ] Should run on `push` to `branches: [ $default-branch ]` and `pull_request` to `branches: [ $default-branch ]`.
- [ ] Packaging workflows should run on `release` with `types: [ created ]`.
- [ ] Publishing workflows should have a filename that is the name of the language or platform, in lower case, followed by "-publish" (for example, [`docker-publish.yml`](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/blob/main/ci/docker-publish.yml)).

**For _Code Scanning_ workflows, the workflow:**

- [ ] Should be preserved under [the `code-scanning` directory](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/tree/main/code-scanning).
- [ ] Should include a matching `code-scanning/properties/*.properties.json` file (for example, [`code-scanning/properties/codeql.properties.json`](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/blob/main/code-scanning/properties/codeql.properties.json)), with properties set as follows:
  - [ ] `name`: Name of the Code Scanning integration.
  - [ ] `creator`: Name of the organization/user producing the Code Scanning integration.
  - [ ] `description`: Short description of the Code Scanning integration.
  - [ ] `categories`: Array of languages supported by the Code Scanning integration.
  - [ ] `iconName`: Name of the SVG logo representing the Code Scanning integration. This SVG logo must be present in [the `icons` directory](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/tree/main/icons).
- [ ] Should run on `push` to `branches: [ $default-branch, $protected-branches ]` and `pull_request` to `branches: [ $default-branch ]`. We also recommend a `schedule` trigger of `cron: $cron-weekly` (for example, [`codeql.yml`](https://github.com/actions/starter-workflows/blob/c59b62dee0eae1f9f368b7011cf05c2fc42cf084/code-scanning/codeql.yml#L14-L21)).

**Some general notes:**

- [ ] This workflow must _only_ use actions that are produced by GitHub, [in the `actions` organization](https://github.com/actions), **or**
- [ ] This workflow must _only_ use actions that are produced by the language or ecosystem that the workflow supports.  These actions must be [published to the GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace?type=actions).  We require that these actions be referenced using the full 40 character hash of the action's commit instead of a tag.  Additionally, workflows must include the following comment at the top of the workflow file:
    ```
    # This workflow uses actions that are not certified by GitHub.
    # They are provided by a third-party and are governed by
    # separate terms of service, privacy policy, and support
    # documentation.
    ```

- [ ] Automation and CI workflows should not send data to any 3rd party service except for the purposes of installing dependencies.

author: ezrosent
body:
These get us pretty close to parity on the `cykjson` benchmark, at least on my machine; I suspect other benchmarks will benefit as well. There are three things going on here:

* Optimizing the process of pushing bindings. This happens quite a lot when there is a large number of matches. The main change is to have a flat representation for bindings, rather than a `DenseIdMap` of `Vec`s. There's also some unsafe code for removing boundschecking, which had a noticeable positive performance impact.
* Managing pending updates via the "frame" subsystem created a lot of repeated allocations and deallocations. This PR flattens the representation of 'frame' into a shared vector.
* It reduces need for `iter_dynamic` over a mask with a macro that special-cases small argument vectors. This was already a technique being used elsewhere in the crate and the macro provides a shared implementation for it.

author: blepping
body:
This pull adds ancestral sampling support as well as an advanced node that exposes the various settings (and allows setting ETA to enable ancestral sampling). The ancestral sampling side works for both flow and non-flow models and was tested on SD 1.5, Wan, Flux, and Cosmos Predict2. These changes should not affect results when ancestral sampling isn't enabled.

I tried to keep these changes minimal and use your code style when possible but a little refactoring was necessary. I also expanded your `first_only` option to allow setting the start/end step ranges for distance sampling.

There's an experimental option to use ancestralness in the internal distance steps as well. Interesting, it works pretty well with flow models (doesn't seem as good with non-flow). Example with Flux, no ancestral sampling:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07c71279-4bab-45f9-947a-0dbb7f26ff19)

vs with these parameters (previous generation was the same, just with both ETA parameters set to 0):

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4bcb9c4a-5985-48a7-bf7f-a58e7060853d)

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3d6bc6d-2cce-484b-b00d-d2bf9e642560)

Hopefully this pull is along the lines of something you'd be interested in merging. If you need anything changed, please let me know!

author: willymwai
body:
This pull request introduces support for the [Flutterwave](https://flutterwave.com/) payment provider across multiple parts of the application. Key changes include adding new GraphQL mutations, models, and services to handle Flutterwave-specific functionality, as well as integrating Flutterwave into existing payment provider workflows.

Flutterwave enables businesses, especially in African countries, to collect payments in local currencies using local payment methods such as:

- Kenya: M‑Pesa, Airtel
- Ghana: MTN, Vodafone, Airtel
- Cameroon: MTN, Orange
- Côte d’Ivoire: MTN, Orange, Moov, Wave
- Senegal: Orange, Free Money, E‑Money, Wave
- Rwanda: Airtel, MTN
- Tanzania: Airtel, Tigo, Halopesa, Vodacom
- Uganda: Airtel, MTN
- Malawi: Airtel Malawi
- Zambia: (through MTN using MPS protocol)

### Flutterwave Payment Provider Integration

#### GraphQL Changes:
* Added `FlutterwaveProvider` type and input object (`app/graphql/types/payment_providers/flutterwave.rb`, `app/graphql/types/payment_providers/flutterwave_input.rb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5be990319d1f926276e3a672a759e9cd2e3c9557e7b34fea0cc6b52d58d9325eR1-R16) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2bebd42563fadd9702a542854d5d0f07a19e881b09e6b485d134f84de0cbe59fR1-R14)
* Introduced mutations for creating and updating Flutterwave payment providers (`app/graphql/mutations/payment_providers/flutterwave/create.rb`, `app/graphql/mutations/payment_providers/flutterwave/update.rb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3dc6c810eb2957798baeddf6d15082b3729ef7d43c32a9c18267913822fb25bdR1-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-37077e21a906b3c66730c01dfd23dcfb10da01d612d4bfe02cf774ec0e0829ebR1-R18)
* Updated `MutationType` and `PaymentProvider` union to include Flutterwave (`app/graphql/types/mutation_type.rb`, `app/graphql/types/payment_providers/object.rb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5e23990e7c2a227e859bf1bdf513b2cf8838c0fe8aa50736ec5cda2a50f454e9R57-R67) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-23d24ab424c8915025a9d413a8c503bcee54aa9b9596f0e70309424faf6f73f2R8-R17) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-23d24ab424c8915025a9d413a8c503bcee54aa9b9596f0e70309424faf6f73f2R28-R29)

#### Controllers and Models:
* Added `flutterwave` method to handle incoming webhooks (`app/controllers/webhooks_controller.rb`).
* Created `FlutterwaveCustomer` and `FlutterwaveProvider` models for payment provider integration (`app/models/payment_provider_customers/flutterwave_customer.rb`, `app/models/payment_providers/flutterwave_provider.rb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-eeaf43f2d2dc62f20e8818a463e6ffe4894ef45d54b7dd27e193e03869f6e45dR1-R9) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a414a7d079b42ff13c72f34ed850a2d8e8f8545948cd12a734b84b495bf42c65R1-R36)
* Updated `Customer` model to include Flutterwave support (`app/models/customer.rb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0c02516694e70a555617bc66660800380a753c26a2d84de824aa9118f0b38aa4R89) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0c02516694e70a555617bc66660800380a753c26a2d84de824aa9118f0b38aa4L97-R98) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0c02516694e70a555617bc66660800380a753c26a2d84de824aa9118f0b38aa4R202-R203)

#### Services:
* Added services for handling Flutterwave payments and customers (`app/services/invoices/payments/flutterwave_service.rb`, `app/services/payment_provider_customers/flutterwave_service.rb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6d81ae88fe10127f27a8df604aee3c868c49a96eb8c7818379cc741430bea68fR1-R181) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b6c2adf1b4cc6d447f134ccbb99072b7e0047da33c10957f0edd54af033bbb68R1-R32)
* Integrated Flutterwave into payment provider factories (`app/services/invoices/payments/payment_providers/factory.rb`, `app/services/payment_provider_customers/factory.rb`, `app/services/payment_providers/create_customer_factory.rb`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-76bb5ecc91da9ba8caf3055162a1b54a4db12897d50fdd95f7de4390874d47bbR21-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-533ea9945385e8708300db1838d01f2b9297d7081958a41532549dce6b6b5f97R17-R18) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-9e2930299fb23179546497344d6eef6793b47b6c6ea3b058da726387b0b378f7R15-R16)

#### Background Jobs:
* Added `HandleEventJob` for processing Flutterwave events asynchronously (`app/jobs/payment_providers/flutterwave/handle_event_job.rb`).

### Other Changes:
* Updated the `Gemfile` to specify platform compatibility for `stackprof` and added `httparty` for HTTP requests (`Gemfile`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d09ea66f8227784ff4393d88a19836f321c915ae10031d16c93d67e6283ab55fR66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d09ea66f8227784ff4393d88a19836f321c915ae10031d16c93d67e6283ab55fL75-R76)

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
# Fix race condition in remote thread list runtime

## Problem
Fixes #2104 - Race condition in `unstable_useRemoteThreadListRuntime` where the first message is not persisted due to timing between `initialize()` and `append()` calls.

The issue occurred because:
1. When a new thread is created, `initialize()` is called asynchronously to get the `remoteId`
2. `append()` is called immediately on the history adapter, but `remoteId` is still empty/undefined
3. The history adapter skips saving the message because there's no `remoteId` yet
4. `initialize()` completes and provides the `remoteId`, but the first message is already lost

## Solution
Created a `BufferedHistoryAdapter` that wraps the base history adapter and:
- Buffers `append()` calls when they occur before initialization completes
- Waits for the `initialize()` promise to resolve and get the `remoteId`
- Flushes all buffered messages to the base history adapter once initialization is complete

## Changes
- **Added**: `packages/react/src/runtimes/remote-thread-list/BufferedHistoryAdapter.tsx` - New adapter that buffers messages until thread initialization
- **Modified**: `packages/react/src/runtimes/remote-thread-list/adapter/cloud.tsx` - Updated to use BufferedHistoryAdapter

- ✅ Code follows existing patterns and conventions
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility

Currently network required for the nodes in defined under zone in CloudstackCluster component like below (network name: capc-network)
```
---
apiVersion: infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta3
kind: CloudStackCluster
metadata:
  name: capc-cluster
  namespace: default
spec:
  controlPlaneEndpoint:
    host: 10.0.56.29
    port: 6443
  failureDomains:
  - acsEndpoint:
      name: secret1
      namespace: default
    name: fd1
    zone:
      name: AdvZone
      network:
        name: capc-network
  syncWithACS: true
---
```
With the new changes multiple networks can be specified at each node specification overriding the zone.network above, for example
```

---
apiVersion: infrastructure.cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta3
kind: CloudStackMachineTemplate
metadata:
  name: capc-cluster-control-plane
  namespace: default
spec:
  template:
```

The unit tests were failing in the GitHub Actions workflow due to a missing GitHub token.

This commit updates the `.github/workflows/pytest-unit-tests.yml` workflow file to include the `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` environment variable in the "Run pytest unit tests" step.

This ensures that the application can authenticate correctly when running in the CI environment, allowing tests that might interact with GitHub features (even if mocked) to pass or behave as expected regarding token presence.

No changes were required in the application or test code as the application is expected to utilize the environment variable if a token is not directly passed during its initialization, and the tests already mock this appropriately.

author: pditommaso
body:
This pull request introduces a new exception, `HttpResponseLengthExceedException`, to enforce a maximum allowed HTTP response size in the `RepositoryProvider` class. It also enhances the `SysEnv` utility to support retrieving integer and long environment variables, and adds comprehensive unit tests for these changes.

### New Exception Handling for HTTP Response Size:

* **New Exception Class**: Added `HttpResponseLengthExceedException` to handle cases where an HTTP response exceeds a configurable maximum size. (`modules/nextflow/src/main/groovy/nextflow/exception/HttpResponseLengthExceedException.groovy`)
* **Integration in `RepositoryProvider`**:
  - Introduced the `checkMaxLength` method in `RepositoryProvider` to validate the `Content-Length` header of HTTP responses against the environment variable `NXF_GIT_RESPONSE_MAX_LENGTH`. (`modules/nextflow/src/main/groovy/nextflow/scm/RepositoryProvider.groovy`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-bca858810859bb18fbb796b959de9fc818664f36c072656396ec2f05eb656331R247) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-bca858810859bb18fbb796b959de9fc818664f36c072656396ec2f05eb656331R316-R326)
  - Updated imports to include the new exception. (`modules/nextflow/src/main/groovy/nextflow/scm/RepositoryProvider.groovy`)

### Enhancements to `SysEnv` Utility:

* **New Methods**: Added `getInteger` and `getLong` methods to retrieve integer and long values from environment variables with optional default values. (`modules/nf-commons/src/main/nextflow/SysEnv.groovy`)

### Unit Tests:

* **Testing `checkMaxLength`**: Added unit tests to validate the behavior of `checkMaxLength` under various scenarios, including when the maximum length is disabled, not set, or exceeded. (`modules/nextflow/src/test/groovy/nextflow/scm/RepositoryProviderTest.groovy`)
* **Testing `SysEnv` Enhancements**: Added unit tests for the new `getInteger` and `getLong` methods to ensure correct parsing of environment variables. (`modules/nf-commons/src/test/nextflow/SysEnvTest.groovy`)

## Summary

This PR implements QA agent integration into the `generateDDLNode` to enable DDL generation from existing schemas. The QA agent analyzes existing schema data and generates PostgreSQL DDL statements for validation and testing purposes.

## Changes Made

### Core Implementation
- **Added QADDLGenerationAgent**: New agent class for DDL generation using LLM
- **Integrated QA agent into generateDDLNode**: Following the established pattern from `designSchemaNode`
- **Added comprehensive prompts**: System prompt for PostgreSQL DDL generation with proper constraints and formatting
- **Proper error handling**: Following established logging and error handling patterns

### Key Features
- Generates DDL statements from existing schema data using `convertSchemaToText` utility
- Uses OpenAI's 'o3' model for high-quality DDL generation
- Includes proper TODO comments indicating LLM-based generation is temporary
- Follows workflow separation: generateDDL generates statements, executeDDL executes them
- Maintains proper state management with `generatedAnswer` for next workflow node

### Files Modified
- `src/chat/workflow/nodes/generateDDLNode.ts` - Main implementation with QA agent integration
- `src/langchain/agents/qaDDLGenerationAgent/` - New agent implementation with prompts
- `src/langchain/agents/index.ts` - Export new agent
- `src/chat/workflow/nodes/validateSchemaNode.ts` - Cleaned up conflicting code

## Technical Details

The implementation follows established patterns:
- Uses the same `ChatAgent` interface as `DatabaseSchemaBuildAgent`
- Leverages existing utilities like `convertSchemaToText`
- Follows prompt template pattern with system and human messages
- Includes proper error handling and state management with logging
- Uses workflow's `formattedHistory` for chat context
- Stores generated DDL in `generatedAnswer` for executeDDLNode to use

- ✅ All linting passes (`pnpm lint`)
- ✅ Code formatting applied (`pnpm fmt`)
- ✅ TypeScript compilation successful
- ✅ Follows established codebase patterns

## Notes

- DDL generation using LLM is marked as temporary solution with TODO comments
- Future implementation will generate DDL mechanically without LLM
- Separation of concerns maintained: generateDDLNode generates, executeDDLNode executes

author: tdruez
body:
### Register a URL to Provide the Challenge

By default, challenge data is generated by the `AltchaField` and embedded directly 
into the rendered HTML using the `challengejson` option.

Alternatively, you can provide a URL that the Altcha widget’s JavaScript will fetch to 
retrieve the challenge, using the `challengeurl` option.

This approach is especially useful for enabling features like `refetchonexpire`, 
which **only work** when using a `challengeurl` (not `challengejson`).

A ready-to-use `AltchaChallengeView` is available in `django_altcha`. 
To enable it, register the view in your `urlpatterns`, for example:

```python
from django.urls import path
from django_altcha import AltchaChallengeView

urlpatterns += [
    path("altcha/challenge/", AltchaChallengeView.as_view(), name="altcha_challenge"),
]
```

Once the URL is registered, you can configure your `AltchaField` to use it via the 
`challengeurl` option:

```python
from django.urls import reverse_lazy
from django import forms
from django_altcha import AltchaField

class MyForm(forms.Form):
    captcha = AltchaField(
        challengeurl=reverse_lazy("altcha_challenge"),
    )
```

> [!NOTE]
> You can customize the challenge generation by passing options directly when 
> registering the view.
> For example: ``AltchaChallengeView.as_view(max_number=2000000)``

author: enricomi
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?
Adds options to retry `FileNotFoundException`s when opening files migrated to the fallback storage.

- `STORAGE_DECOMMISSION_FALLBACK_STORAGE_REPLICATION_DELAY` sets the allowed replication delay.
The executor waits at most this long for the shuffle data file to appear on the fallback storage
- `STORAGE_DECOMMISSION_FALLBACK_STORAGE_REPLICATION_WAIT` sets an interval of re-attempts looking for the file

### Why are the changes needed?
Using a distributed filesystem as the fallback storage for migrating shuffle data on executor decommissioning, executors that attempt to read the migrated data might not yet see the file that has been written by the decommissioned executor. This is called replication delay.

Currently, executors give up instantly, even though they know the data have been successfully migrated to the fallback storage, from where they do not migrate further. Having the executor wait for a defined time and reattempt to open the file avoids a fetch failure and a re-computation of the migrated shuffle data.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
No

### How was this patch tested?
Unit test.

author: treff7es
body:
# Apache Airflow 3.x Support - PR Description

## Summary

This PR adds comprehensive Apache Airflow 3.x support to the DataHub Airflow plugin while maintaining full backward compatibility with Airflow 2.7+. The implementation uses separate, version-specific code paths to ensure type safety and maintainability.

## Key Changes

### 🏗️ Architecture: Separate Version-Specific Implementations

The plugin now uses distinct implementations for each Airflow major version:

| Component               | Airflow 2.x                        | Airflow 3.x                                                     |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Main Module**         | `airflow2/datahub_listener.py`     | `airflow3/datahub_listener.py`                                  |
| **Shims/Imports**       | `airflow2/_shims.py`               | `airflow3/_shims.py`                                            |
| **Lineage Extraction**  | Extractor-based (`_extractors.py`) | Unified SQLParser patch (`_airflow3_sql_parser_patch.py`)       |
| **OpenLineage Package** | `openlineage-airflow>=1.2.0`       | Native provider (`apache-airflow-providers-openlineage>=1.0.0`) |
| **Type Checking**       | ✅ Clean Airflow 2.x types         | ✅ Clean Airflow 3.x types                                      |

**Benefits:**

- ✅ **Type Safety** - Each version properly type-checked against its respective Airflow API
- ✅ **Maintainability** - No complex version conditionals scattered throughout
- ✅ **Clarity** - Clear separation of version-specific logic
- ✅ **Testing** - Each version tested independently

### 📦 Installation Requirements (Breaking Change)

Users must now specify version-appropriate extras when installing:

```bash
# For Airflow 2.7+
pip install 'acryl-datahub-airflow-plugin[airflow2]'

# For Airflow 3.x
pip install 'acryl-datahub-airflow-plugin[airflow3]'
```

**What gets installed:**

- **Base (no extra):** Core plugin + `acryl-datahub[sql-parser,datahub-rest]` + `pydantic>=2.4.0` + `apache-airflow>=2.5.0` (no OpenLineage package)
- **`[airflow2]` extra:** Adds `openlineage-airflow>=1.2.0` (standalone package for Airflow 2.x)
- **`[airflow3]` extra:** Adds `apache-airflow-providers-openlineage>=1.0.0` (native provider for Airflow 3.x)

**Airflow 3.0.x Note:** Requires manual pydantic upgrade due to Airflow 3.0.6 bug:

```bash
pip install 'acryl-datahub-airflow-plugin[airflow3]' 'pydantic>=2.11.8'
```

**Breaking Change:** Installing without the appropriate extra means you must provide your own OpenLineage package. The plugin will auto-detect which OpenLineage variant is available and use it accordingly.

### 📊 Compatibility Matrix

| Airflow Version | Extra to Install | Status                 | Notes                             |
| --------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| 2.7-2.10        | `[airflow2]`     | ✅ Fully Supported     | Use `openlineage-airflow` package |
| 3.0.x           | `[airflow3]`     | ⚠️ Requires manual fix | Needs `pydantic>=2.11.8` upgrade  |
| 3.1+            | `[airflow3]`     | ✅ Fully Supported     | Native OpenLineage provider       |

**Note:** Airflow versions prior to 2.7 are no longer supported. The last version supporting Airflow 2.5-2.6 was DataHub 1.1.x.

## Technical Improvements

### 1. Unified SQLParser Patch (Airflow 3.x)

**The most significant architectural change** is how lineage extraction works in Airflow 3.x:

| Aspect                  | Airflow 2.x                     | Airflow 3.x                            |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- |
| **Lineage Extraction**  | Operator-specific extractors    | Unified SQLParser patch                |
| **Customization Point** | Custom extractor per operator   | Single SQL parser integration          |
| **Column Lineage**      | Extractor-dependent             | ✅ Consistent across ALL SQL operators |
| **Maintenance**         | Multiple extractors to maintain | Single integration point               |

**In Airflow 2.x:**

```python
# Different extractor for each SQL operator
SnowflakeExtractor, PostgresExtractor, MySQLExtractor, etc.
```

**In Airflow 3.x:**

```python
# Single patch point for ALL SQL operators
SQLParser.generate_openlineage_metadata_from_sql = datahub_enhanced_version
```

**Benefits:**

- ✅ **Better consistency** - All SQL operators use the same lineage extraction logic
- ✅ **Easier maintenance** - One integration point instead of many extractors
- ✅ **Column-level lineage for all** - Works across all SQL operators uniformly
- ✅ **Future-proof** - New SQL operators automatically get DataHub lineage
- ✅ **Custom operator support** - Any operator using OpenLineage's SQLParser gets DataHub's enhancements automatically

### 2. SDK Connection API Migration

Migrated from deprecated `BaseHook.get_connection()` to the official `airflow.sdk.Connection.get()` API:

**Why this matters:**

- ✅ Works in all contexts (listener hooks, task execution, DAG parsing)
- ✅ No `SUPERVISOR_COMMS` dependency required
- ✅ Uses official Airflow 3.x SDK (not deprecated)
- ✅ More reliable connection retrieval

### 3. Robust URL Parsing

Replaced manual string concatenation with `urllib.parse` for connection URLs:

**Benefits:**

- ✅ Handles IPv6 addresses correctly
- ✅ Preserves URL paths and query strings
- ✅ Proper port handling
- ✅ Follows URL standards

### 4. Kill Switch Migration

The plugin's disable mechanism now uses different approaches based on Airflow version:

**Airflow 2.x:**

```bash
# Use Airflow Variable (database-backed)
airflow variables set datahub_airflow_plugin_disable_listener true
```

**Airflow 3.x:**

```bash
# Use environment variable (required due to database access restrictions)
export AIRFLOW_VAR_DATAHUB_AIRFLOW_PLUGIN_DISABLE_LISTENER=true
```

**Reason:** Airflow 3.x prohibits database writes in listener hooks to prevent HA lock issues. `Variable.get()` creates a database session commit, which breaks this restriction.

### 5. Appropriate Log Level Adjustments

Reduced noise in production logs:

- Changed debug-level messages in patch modules to use `logger.debug()` instead of `logger.info()`
- Reduced per-task logging verbosity
- Cleaner production log output while preserving debugging capability when needed

### 6. Enhanced Documentation

Added comprehensive documentation for users:

**Installation Dependencies:**

- Clear breakdown of what gets installed with each extra (`[airflow2]`, `[airflow3]`, or base installation)
- Detailed explanation of OpenLineage package differences between versions

**Custom Operators with OpenLineage:**

- New section showing how to create custom SQL operators that implement OpenLineage's standard interface
- Demonstrates how the SQLParser patch automatically provides column-level lineage
- Shows operators work with both pure OpenLineage AND DataHub without vendor lock-in
- Provides working examples for both OpenLineage-based and manual lineage approaches

## Airflow 3.x Specific Changes

### Import Path Updates

Airflow 3.x reorganized modules under new SDK structure. The plugin uses version-specific shims:

```python
# Airflow 3.x
from airflow.sdk.bases.operator import BaseOperator
from airflow.providers.standard.operators.empty import EmptyOperator

# Airflow 2.x
from airflow.models.baseoperator import BaseOperator
from airflow.operators.empty import EmptyOperator
```

### DAG Parameter Changes

1. **Schedule Parameter:**

   - `schedule_interval` → `schedule` (supported in Airflow 2.4+, required in 3.x)

2. **Default View Removed:**
   - `default_view` parameter no longer accepted in Airflow 3.x
   - User preferences

author: chdh-odoo
body: **Purpose:** Improved redirect rule logic to allow applying rules based on user's groups. Added a selection with 3 options: all users, if has group, or if not in group. This gives more control over redirect behavior. **Approach:** Added a selection field 'User groups' with 3 options: - All users: rule applies to everyone - In group: applies only if user belongs to listed groups - Not in group: applies only if user does NOT belong to them Used this selection to dynamically filter redirects based on current user's group. **For 301/302 (page-level) rules**: group checks are done in runtime via _serve_redirect method. **For 404 (route-level) rules**: routing map is precomputed inside _generate_routing_rules, so we can't check groups directly. To solve this, added a middleware route: conditional_redirect. In _generate_routing_rules, if any URL has a redirect rule written, we attach this middleware endpoint to the route. At runtime, the request hits middleware first. It checks current user groups and decides whether to apply the redirect or let the normal flow continue. Example: a 404 rule is set on /shop only if user belongs to the 'Non-Shopkeeper' group. When routing map is generated, it iterates over each route. If it finds a rule for /shop, it attaches /shop to the conditional_redirect middleware route endpoint. At runtime, when a request comes to /shop, it first goes to the middleware. It checks if the current user has the 'Non-Shopkeeper' group. If yes, the user is redirected to 404 page. If not, the request flows to /shop as normal. Doing this for a 308 redirect is not a good idea, as each route is served using a precomputed routing map that caches the endpoints. Additionally, it includes validations like slug matching, Altering the current implementation of routes from precomputed to runtime is not a feasible idea Preview: task-3861441

author: rovo89
body:
Several people complained that the mower leaves some space between the lines uncut:
https://discord.com/channels/958476543846412329/961804411112394842/1382596496498626672
https://discord.com/channels/958476543846412329/1079054431758332027/1381680934859833464
https://discord.com/channels/958476543846412329/961804411112394842/1380152880165814322

I noticed it for myself as well, but blamed it on the wheels pushing the grass down. I finally did some investigations using my [SVG plotter](https://github.com/rovo89/open_mower_ros/commits/svg/) and an artificial area of 1x2 m and could confirm the issue there.

Here are the plans for 10cm / 20cm / 40cm distance without any outlines:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0fb118f4-8e29-4714-b516-94590da7c13a)
5.01 / 16.26 / 27.5 / 38.75 / 50.0 / 61.25 / 72.5 / 83.74 / 94.99

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/916d9749-cf6a-4209-b064-588e18abdc9e)
10.01 / 34.01 / 58.01 / 82.01 / 90.0

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f1e177-7a29-4f2c-914a-b750e892e019)
20.01 / 68.01 / 80.0

It's clearly visible that the distance is wrong (11.25 / 24 / 48 cm).

---

Then I found out about this parameter:
```
bool Slic3r::Fill::dont_adjust
Don't adjust spacing to fill the space evenly.
```

Which was set to "false" since 2021 with an explanation of "wip": https://github.com/ClemensElflein/slic3r_coverage_planner/commit/6a10099b311505f437a330f3df32131309633a7b

If set it to "true, i.e. disable adjustments and ask it to use exactly the provided distance, the results are almost as expected:
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a30d89ee-f677-44fd-b111-bc3c626bf849)
10.0 / 20.0 / 30.0 / 40.0 / 50.0 / 60.0 / 70.0 / 80.0 / 90.0

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4352c2eb-56f8-4e5b-8cd6-84ce00cc0b04)
10.0 / 30.0 / 50.0 / 70.0 / 90.0

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6848c5df-df98-40c8-90e7-f449028ba652)
20.0 / 50.0

---

Almost good, but the 40 cm distance can't fill the 100 cm even and that causes unmowed space at end... and I have no idea why it doesn't go to 20/60 cm, leaving 20 instead of 30 cm unmowed.

I'm not sure if this can be solved with slic3r. The solution would probably be to mow the last line with a bit more overlap, which 3D printers probably won't do. Alternatively, we could try to calculate a spacing which equal to or slightly smaller than the configured tool width. But that's not correct either. 33.3333 cm seems like the answer, for which we get 0.167 / 0.5 / 0.833. That's three lines which is the perfect number of lines mowed to cover 100 cm width a 40 cm tool, but it goes beyond the outline a bit. Might be acceptable for outline_count > 0. We'd need to redo some of the work of the slic3r to figure out the total width (seems to be the bounding box after rotating). 

---

Even with this remaining issue, I think it's better than before, because we no longer have a lot of uncut area between the lines, just some in the beginning and/or end.

author: tieukhoimai
body:
## AnalyticsAgent Features

- **Data Loading & Resampling:** Loads CSV data for factory components, filters by time range, and resamples using appropriate aggregation (mean, max, or mode) based on data type.
- **Component Configuration:** Supports multiple factory components (e.g., VGR, HBW, MPO, SLD, ENVIRONMENTAL) with flexible file mapping and descriptions.
- **Metrics & Summaries:** Calculates metrics such as activity percentages, position ranges, and environmental statistics for each component.
- **Cycle Analysis:** Detects manufacturing process cycles, identifies per-cycle types, and tracks active components.
- **Natural Language Query Support:** Parses user queries to extract time ranges and relevant components, enabling flexible and intuitive data analysis.
- **LLM-Powered Explanations:** Generates comprehensive process explanations using large language models, based on chart images and data summaries.
- **Chart Generation:** Creates and saves visualizations for factory overview, component activity, and environmental data.
- **Error Handling:** Provides clear feedback for missing or invalid data.

## UI Capabilities

- **Interactive Dashboard:** Displays metrics, summaries, and charts for selected components and time ranges.
- **Natural Language Interface:** Users can input queries like "Show environmental data for last 10 minutes" or "Analyze VGR activity on 2/12/2022 from 14:00 to 14:30".
- **Dynamic Chart Rendering:** Visualizes data interactively based on query context (component and time range).
- **Process Insights:** Presents LLM-generated explanations and cycle analysis results for deeper understanding of factory operations.
- **Component Selection:** Allows users to select specific components or view overall factory metrics.

These features enable users to explore, analyze, and visualize manufacturing data efficiently, with advanced support for natural language

author: dominiklohmann
body:
This change improves the performance of deeply nested chains of `and` and `or`, which previously had a cascading effect of sliced batches. Now, each `and` / `or` expression returns just a single series.

Note that this is far from perfect—an ideal solution would avoid slicing in the first place, and instead pass through a validity bitmap. However, that would require touching every single function we have to support this, which I'd like to avoid.

In a very much non-scientific benchmark on a node with the demo-node dataset imported, this decreased the time spent in `where` by 28% for me locally for this pipeline:

```
export
this = this # prevent predicate pushdown
where @name == "zeek.conn" and id.orig_h in 209.0.0.0/8 and id.orig_p > 40000 or id.resp_p < 200
discard
```

author: maciejbalanv
body:
This PR adds a CLI arguments `--offload_guardrail` and `--offload_prompt_refiner`  to control offloading of guardrails and prompt refiner in `examples/text2image.py` and `examples/text2video.py` scripts. Previously we only had this option in `examples/video2world.py` script. 

Additionally, same as for `examples/video2world.py`, the offloading will be now disabled by default and we'll need to pass this option if we want to enable offloading. The offloading is not needed on most of data-center GPUs, especially for 2B models, and having it enabled by default can unnecessarily hurt performance. The current benchmarking numbers we have were done with offloading disabled.

author: fornellas
body:
We randomly hit this case:

```
  🖥 Host
    type: ssh
    name: n2p.local
    DEBUG Close
  ERROR failed to close host
    error:
      failed to run /tmp/resonance_agent.L1IPYkml : write |1: broken pipe
      Process did not exit:
```

Root cause seems to be race condition between the gRPC client & server, which have left over bufferett things that attempt to go through the SSH session that's ended when the process exits.

This PR changes the shutdown mechanics:

- It asks the agent to shutdown itself by calling the CLI again, and the CLI identifies running process, and asks for them to stop gracefully.
- It makes the agent remove itself, so there's no junk left behind (tangent bug also fixed).

## 📌 이슈 번호
- #39 

## 👩🏻‍💻 구현 내용
### Problem
- 메인골 리스트 조회 api에서 다음과 같은 문제점이 있었음.
  - 대표 여부에 대한 응답 미포함
  - `main_goal_` 접두사를 붙인 flat한 구조
  - 공통 응답 포맷을 사용하지 않았음.
  ```json
    [
      {
        "main_goal_id":1,
        "main_goal_name":"예제메인골1",
        "main_goal_status":"ACTIVITY"
      },
      {
        "main_goal_id":2,
        "main_goal_name":"예제메인골2",
        "main_goal_status":"ACTIVITY"
      }
    ]
   ```

### Approach
- 대표 여부에 대한 응답을 `is_rep`(key), `Boolean`(value)로 반환
- `main_goals` 키로 리스트를 감싸 구조화 ➡️ 데이터 의미 명확화 + 가독성 향상
- 공통 응답 포맷 적용
  ```json
  {
    "code": "200",
    "message": "success",
    "data": {
      "main_goals": [
        {
          "id": 1,
          "name": "string",
          "status": "ACTIVITY",
          "is_rep": true
        },
        {
          "id": 2,
          "name": "string1",
          "status": "ACTIVITY",
          "is_rep": false
        }
      ]
   }
  }
  ```

author: bd1976bris
body:
8.3-style short-form paths (e.g., C:\PROGRA~1) can cause inconsistencies or
failures on remote machines during distributed linking. Such paths may not
resolve correctly or may differ between systems. Short-form paths are
relatively common - for example, clang often writes temporary object files
to %TEMP%, which is frequently a short-form path.

We are aware of at least one distribution system (SN-DBS) affected by this,
and we expect that many (perhaps all) distribution systems may encounter
similar issues.

This patch ensures that all Windows paths used for DTLTO in ELF LLD are
normalized to their long form using GetLongPathNameW. This avoids ambiguity
and improves portability across distribution environments.

For testing, AreShortNamesEnabled is used to detect whether 8.3 path support
is enabled on the current volume. However, this API is only available on
Windows 11. As a result, the related tests are skipped on earlier versions
of Windows due to the lack of a reliable alternative for feature detection.

author: vincent-pochet
body:
Reapply https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/pull/3839 that was rollbacked to allow a non blocking release

## Context

As we are planing to release the ["not null organization" pull request](https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/pull/3687), it was decided to take this as an opportunity to squash the old database migration into a single migration file, to reduce the number of migrations.

Related to https://github.com/getlago/lago-api/pull/3829

## Description

Lago version 1.20.0 was used as a reference to squash the migrations.

- All migrations from previous versions are merged in a single `InitialMigration` migration file. 
  - It uses the SQL format to preserve the orders and make sure the migration test workflow continue to pass on Github no matter if the structure comes from previous migrations or from this file.
  - It reuse the previous last migration version `20250122112050` to make sure it will not be executed on instance running v1.20.0 or later.
  - It adds a small check to fail running the migration if an upgrade is made from a version prior to 1.20.0 to the bridge release containing this change
- All squashed migrations files are removed
